l-aventure-ambigue: A boy seen from behind sits by a wood fire in a Sahelian Koranic school courtyard at dawn, a wooden tablet on his knees; far beyond the dunes, the faint grey rooftops and spires of a European city dissolve into mist.
les-bouts-de-bois-de-dieu: A crowded railway workshop in Thiès in 1947, idle locomotives cooling on the rails, women in long wrappers carrying water jugs on their heads along the tracks, a huge red sun hanging over the silent strike.
ethiopiques: A kora and a talking drum resting on a woven mat under a starry West African night, a baobab silhouetted against the moon, and on the far horizon the glowing towers of New York rising like a dream.
la-plus-secrete-memoire-des-hommes: A young man seen from behind in a dim Paris attic, holding a worn leather-bound volume with a blank cover; beyond the window, layered horizons of Senegalese coast, French rooftops and Argentine pampas fade into one another.
le-ventre-de-l-atlantique: The small island of Niodior at dusk, mangroves and pirogues on the shore, a boy seen from behind kicking a football on the sand, while across the immense Atlantic a faint cold European city glimmers.
murambi-le-livre-des-ossements: A silent hilltop school in the green Rwandan hills, empty classrooms with open doors, abandoned shoes and folded cloths lined up on a bench, a lone figure seen from afar walking up the red dirt path under a pale sky.
la-greve-des-battu: A sunlit Dakar street emptied of beggars, a row of abandoned wooden alms bowls along a whitewashed wall, an official black car parked in the distance, the minaret of a mosque shimmering in the heat.
frere-d-ame: A muddy First World War trench under a grey sky, a lone Senegalese rifleman seen from behind in a red chechia looking over the barbed wire, a memory of a sunlit Sahel village floating in the clouds above.
les-contes-d-amadou-koumba: A night gathering under a great baobab, an old griot seen from behind telling tales by a fire, while in the shadows a clever hare and a hungry hyena tiptoe through the tall grass under the moon.
le-baobab-fou: A lone, twisted baobab in the dry Senegalese plain at noon, a little girl seen from behind standing in its shade, and beyond, a grey rainy Brussels street with tram lines drifting like a mirage.
trois-femmes-puissantes: Three women seen from behind, each in a different place: a garden with a flame tree in Dakar, a grey French suburban house, a dusty road toward the desert; a single bird soars above all three.
afrotopia: A luminous imagined African city growing organically from the land, earthen domes and green terraces, rivers and gardens, people walking from afar along tree-lined paths, a wide golden sunrise on the horizon.
nations-negres-et-culture: The Nile flowing from the green heart of Africa to the pyramids of ancient Egypt, carved sphinxes, papyrus reeds and baobabs on the same riverbank, a soft dawn light uniting the whole continent.
amkoullel-l-enfant-peul: A Malian village on the Niger in the early twentieth century, a small boy seen from behind sitting among elders under a tree, cattle and Fulani herders at the river, a colonial school building white in the distance.
l-etrange-destin-de-wangrin: A colonial-era administrative veranda in French West Africa, a man in a white boubou seen from behind standing between an empty colonial chair with a pith helmet and a group of village chiefs seen from afar, a sly glint of sunlight.
le-devoir-de-violence: An imaginary Sahelian kingdom over centuries: a fortified earthen palace with tall towers under a blood-orange sky, long shadows of horsemen crossing the dunes, and on the horizon a colonial flagpole rising.
l-enfant-noir: A blacksmith's forge in Kouroussa glowing in the dusk, gold melting in a small crucible, a little black snake coiled near the anvil, a boy seen from behind watching from the doorway.
le-roi-de-kahel: The green plateaus and waterfalls of the Fouta-Djalon at the end of the nineteenth century, a lone European explorer in a pith helmet seen from far behind on horseback, facing a hilltop Fulani village of round thatched huts.
soundjata-ou-l-epopee-mandingue: A thirteenth-century Mandinka landscape at dawn, a crooked iron staff and a young boy seen from behind rising from the ground beside a great baobab, horsemen's banners of the Mali empire glowing in the distance.
les-soleils-des-independances: A proud old prince seen from behind in a faded embroidered boubou walking alone along a dusty avenue of a newly independent West African capital, party banners without words fluttering, a heavy setting sun.
allah-n-est-pas-oblige: A small boy seen from behind walking along a red laterite road through the West African forest beside an old man carrying amulets and a bundle, a burned-out truck and abandoned sandals on the roadside, smoke on the horizon.
reine-pokou: A wide, roaring river at twilight, a crowd of people seen from behind gathered on the bank, a queen in a golden wrapper standing at the front with arms raised, great trees bending over the water to form a bridge.
climbie: A colonial classroom in Côte d'Ivoire, rows of wooden benches, a small object hanging from a string around a boy's neck seen from behind, a lagoon and palm trees visible through the open window.
le-pagne-noir: An orphan girl seen from behind kneeling by a forest stream, washing a black cloth in the clear water, while a clever spider dangles from a branch above and the moonlight turns the river silver.
debout-paye: A security guard seen from behind standing motionless in the bright doorway of a glossy Paris perfume shop, shoppers flowing past as blurred silhouettes, the Seine and Haussmann rooftops beyond the glass.
le-tambour-des-larmes: A young woman seen from behind fleeing across the Mauritanian desert at night, a large sacred drum strapped on her back, nomad tents and camels left far behind, the lights of a city on the horizon.
crepuscule-des-temps-anciens: A village of the Bwa people in old Burkina Faso at twilight, earthen houses with flat roofs, leaf masks dancing in a circle around a fire, millet fields glowing gold under the setting sun.
un-piege-sans-fin: A herder seen from behind leading zebu cattle across the wide savannah of northern Dahomey, a lone fig tree, storm clouds gathering over the path ahead that coils like a spiral into the distance.
place-des-fetes: A young man seen from behind sitting on the steps of a Paris suburban housing block, an African village of mud houses and palm trees projected like a faded dream onto the concrete walls, evening neon lights.
le-pauvre-christ-de-bomba: A missionary's bicycle and a boy carrying a heavy trunk on his head walking away along a red forest track in southern Cameroon in the 1930s, a small wooden chapel among giant trees, an empty village beyond.
une-vie-de-boy: A colonial residence veranda in Cameroon at dusk, a set table with white porcelain and a pith helmet on a chair, a houseboy seen from behind holding a tray, a small notebook tucked in his apron pocket.
les-honneurs-perdus: A woman in a bright wax dress seen from behind, a small suitcase in hand, leaving a crowded Douala neighbourhood of tin roofs, while the grey streets and colourful markets of Paris Belleville rise before her.
la-saison-de-l-ombre: A Central African forest village at night after a fire, charred huts and smoke drifting, a single woman seen from behind walking into the dark forest, a pale moon over a distant ocean shore.
les-impatientes: A walled courtyard in northern Cameroon, three women seen from behind in richly coloured veils sitting apart from one another, a closed carved wooden door, the hot Sahelian sky and a single bird on the wall.
temps-de-chien: A lively neighbourhood bar in Yaoundé at night, a dog lying at the foot of a wooden counter watching the scene, beer bottles, plastic chairs and silhouetted customers arguing under a bare light bulb.
les-maquisards: A dense equatorial forest in Bassa country in the 1950s, a woman seen from behind carrying a basket of food along a hidden path, a secret camp of palm-leaf shelters glimpsed among the giant trees.
critique-de-la-raison-negre: Broken iron chains lying on a beach at dusk, a slave ship fading on the horizon, the silhouette of a modern global city rising from the sea, and a single sprout growing through the rusted links.
memoires-de-porc-epic: A porcupine sitting at the foot of a huge baobab under the full moon, its quills glowing, a Congolese village sleeping in the distance and a man's shadow stretching across the path.
la-vie-et-demie: A grand, decaying presidential palace of an imaginary African country, a long empty banquet table with candles, a ghostly translucent figure seen from behind standing at the far end, red curtains and a stormy sky.
johnny-chien-mechant: A deserted African capital during a civil war, smoke rising over tin roofs, an abandoned wheelbarrow with a bundle of belongings on a road, a girl seen from behind pushing it toward the forest.
le-pleurer-rire: A lavish post-independence presidential reception hall, an empty gilded throne-like chair, a laden banquet table with champagne, a butler seen from behind holding a silver tray, a carnival mask lying on the floor.
congo-inc: A young man seen from behind with a backpack leaving the equatorial forest for Kinshasa, the river Congo shining, chaotic streets, mining trucks, satellite dishes and a glowing smartphone in his hand.
tram-83: A neon-lit nightclub in a mining town that never sleeps, a crowded dance floor of silhouettes, a saxophone and trumpet in the haze, mine shafts and red earth visible through the open doors at night.
notre-dame-du-nil: An isolated girls' boarding school on a misty ridge in the Rwandan hills, schoolgirls in blue uniforms seen from behind walking in line toward a chapel, the source of the Nile trickling below.
jacaranda: A jacaranda tree in full violet bloom over a garden in Kigali, fallen purple petals on a red path, a man seen from behind looking toward the green hills of the reborn city at sunset.
aux-etats-unis-d-afrique: A reversed world: a rich, gleaming African metropolis with golden towers and green gardens on one shore, and on the other, ruined grey European cities, small boats crossing the sea toward Africa at dawn.
eve-de-ses-decombres: A poor neighbourhood of Port-Louis, grey concrete blocks and corrugated iron, four teenagers seen from behind sitting on a wall, the turquoise sea and mountains of Mauritius far beyond.
tropique-de-la-violence: A shanty town of tin and tarpaulin on a hillside in Mayotte, a boy seen from behind standing alone on the slope, the blue lagoon and a small migrant boat on the horizon at sunset.
presque-songes: The high plateaus of Madagascar at night, terraced rice fields under a vast starry sky, ancestral stone tombs, a crescent moon and a mythical bird gliding through dreamlike clouds.
nour-1947: A dense Malagasy rainforest at night in 1947, a man seen from behind sitting beside a figure shrouded in white cloth, a small fire, giant ferns and lemurs watching from the branches.
anguille-sous-roche: A young woman swimming alone in a vast turquoise sea between the islands of the Comoros, seen from above, her wrapper floating around her, a volcanic island and a small mosque on the distant shore.
rever-en-temps-de-guerre: A small boy seen from behind sitting on a hill in Limuru, a book on his knees, tea plantations and red earth below, colonial trucks on a distant road and stormy clouds gathering over Kenya.
disgrace: An isolated farmhouse in the dry Eastern Cape, a man seen from behind with a suitcase walking toward it, dogs in kennels, aloe plants and wide hills under a harsh white sky.
un-long-chemin-vers-la-liberte: A barred window of a small prison cell on an island, the sea and Table Mountain beyond, a beam of dawn light falling on a stone floor and a long winding road stretching toward the horizon.
le-monde-s-effondre: An Igbo village compound of red mud and thatch, yam fields and a wrestling ground, a tall man seen from behind standing at the edge, while a white mission church appears on the distant hill under gathering clouds.
l-autre-moitie-du-soleil: A house in Nsukka in the 1960s with a garden of flame trees, a boy seen from behind sweeping the porch, and on the horizon a half-rising yellow sun on a red and black sky.
no-home: A white colonial fort on the Gold Coast at sunset, the ocean crashing on the rocks, two paths diverging from the gate, one toward a sunlit balcony, the other toward a dark stone archway opening onto the sea.
aya-de-yopougon: A lively Abidjan neighbourhood at night in the late 1970s, three young women seen from behind in colourful outfits walking toward a music-filled maquis, string lights, palm trees and a crowded street.
akissi: A little girl seen from behind running barefoot through a sunny Abidjan courtyard, chasing a cat between laundry lines and plastic buckets, neighbours peeking from doorways, a big mango tree.
la-vie-de-pahe: A small town in northern Gabon, a boy seen from behind running with friends along a red dirt road toward a school, a family house with a corrugated iron roof and tall equatorial forest behind.
dipoula: An orphanage courtyard run by nuns in Gabon, a little boy with a straw hat seen from behind playing with a band of friends, white walls, a bell tower and a mango tree in the bright sunlight.
petit-joss: A primary school in Douala in the 1970s, a sunny schoolyard with children seen from behind running toward a vegetable garden, a strange eclipse darkening the sky over the classroom roof.
tempete-sur-bangui: The city of Bangui under a heavy stormy sky in 2012, empty streets, closed shutters, smoke on the horizon, and a desk by a window with drawing paper and pencils lit by a single candle.
madame-livingstone: Lake Tanganyika in 1915, an old biplane flying low over the water, a silhouetted man in a Scottish kilt and another in an aviator's jacket seen from behind on the shore, a distant warship on the horizon.
malamine: A man seen from behind in a neat suit standing alone on a grey Paris metro platform, a briefcase in hand, crowds rushing past as blurred silhouettes, a warm African sunset reflected in the train window.
rwanda-1994: Green terraced hills of Rwanda in April 1994, an empty house with an open door, a mother's patterned wrapper caught on a fence, children's sandals on the path, dark clouds gathering over the hills.
une-eternite-a-tanger: A young man seen from behind sitting on a rock above the port of Tanger at night, looking across the narrow strait toward the twinkling lights of Spain, a small bundle at his feet.
